title: Arthur Fils breaks through with historic Cincinnati Open triumph
content:
Arthur Fils has been flashing warning signs for some time now. All year, the 22-year-old Frenchman has been excelling at Masters 1000 tournaments, the events played one level below a Grand Slam, wielding his hammer of a forehand and running his opponents into the ground.

Never mind that he was sidelined with an injury from last May until February. Never mind that he’s missed four of the last five major tournaments. Few on the ATP tour this year have made better use of their time on court.

After reaching two Masters 1000 semifinals this year, Fils finally broke through to win the biggest title of his career Sunday, beating Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 1-6, 6-0 in a final for the history books at the Cincinnati Open. It was the first ATP Masters 1000 final contested between two Black players since the tournament series began in 1990.

It was also the first ATP Masters 1000 title won by a French player since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in Toronto in 2014.

“First, I have to start with you Frances,” Fils said in his winner’s speech. “It’s good to be here playing a final against you. When I was young, I was watching you a lot on TV. You are one of the guys that was making me turn on the TV, so I’m very happy to see you back on that level and I hope we’re going to have a lot of nice (matches).”

Fils’ victory was lopsided and full of the tennis that has fans so excited about his future on tour.

Tiafoe took a medical timeout between the second and third set to get the area around his right lower back or hip worked on and was clearly struggling throughout the third set. But Fils still had a chance to show off his audacious tennis, mostly in the first set, when he charged out to a 3-0 lead. He dictated with his topspin-heavy forehand, pinpoint serving, and aggressive choices that kept Tiafoe on his heels.

He won 12 of the first 13 points and had the first set sewn up in a blink, 28 minutes. His level dipped in the second set to give Tiafoe a chance to make it a match, but the American was so hampered that the third set was never truly in question.

For Fils, just making Sunday’s final is a testament to his impressive ability to bounce back, a gift born of a unique blend of a positive mindset, fearlessness and sheer talent.

In May of 2025, the Frenchman suffered a stress fracture in his back that forced him to retire in the second round of the French Open and kept him off the court for nine months until February of this year. He used the time away to tighten his forehand and serve, and improved his movement such that when he returned, he wasn’t rusty — he had upgraded.

That led to an improbable run where Fils made it to the final of a 500-level tournament in Doha, a quarterfinal and two semifinal appearances at 1000-level tournaments and a title at the 500-level Barcelona Open before the injury bug bit again. Fils hurt his hip in the opening round of the Italian Open in May, forcing him to miss his home Grand Slam once again.

Again, he sat out, and again, he returned with force. After a second-round exit at Wimbledon and first-round loss at the D.C. Open, Fils made it to the quarterfinals of the Masters 1000 in Montreal before making the biggest final of his career, some 15 months after that initial stress fracture in his back.

He is 4-2 in his last six matches against top-10 opponents and will rise to a career-high No. 11 in the world Monday as he heads into the U.S. Open with five career titles and a chance to make an impression in front of the biggest crowds in tennis.

The opportunity that awaits him is massive, because world No. 1 Jannik Sinner is out of the tournament and defending champion Carlos Alcaraz is coming back from a wrist injury, but also because the crowds in New York are exactly the type to fall in love with Fils’ athletic, big, daring game. It helps that the Frenchman doesn’t hide his personality on court, pumping himself up with positive self-talk. He isn’t afraid to engage the crowd.

Perhaps they’ll even forgive him for his 8-0 record against Americans dating back to the start of the 2025 season.

Tiafoe was looking to become the first American men’s champion in Cincinnati since Andy Roddick in 2006. Instead, Fils made good on all the promise he showed earlier this year. He is the youngest ATP Masters 1000 champion from France in series history.
